what: Lennar is one of the largest American homebuilders by deliveries. It builds homes across most major US markets and also originates mortgages and provides title insurance for its own buyers.
customers: First-time and move-up home buyers across the United States.
money: mortgage origination and title services for its own buyers
moat: Scale that lowers cost per home, and a shift to controlling land through options rather than owning it, which reduces the capital at risk in a downturn.
risks: High mortgage rates have slowed sales and forced heavy price incentives
Buying down buyers' mortgage rates eats into gross margin
Analyst targets imply the shares are above fair value
opportunities: It spun off its land holdings into a separate company, making the builder lighter on capital
Debt of about $6 billion against $1.5 billion of cash is manageable
Lower mortgage rates would revive demand quickly
watch: New orders, deliveries, and gross margin after incentives.
